_note: Synthetic. The autonomy ladder of the fictional company Halden Industrial: which ticket types may be worked at which level. Every threshold here is an assumption, chosen to be plausible, not measured. A company enters its own. Changing this file changes what an agent may do, without changing code.

levels.name: Watch
levels.the_agent_may: Read the ticket and write down what it would have done. The note is kept for comparison and is not shown to the person working the ticket.
levels.a_case_is_checked_by: Comparing the agent's note with what the person did.

levels.name: Propose
levels.the_agent_may: Put a proposed fix in front of the person working the ticket, who carries it out or not.
levels.a_case_is_checked_by: Whether the person carried out the proposal unchanged, and whether the fix held.

levels.name: Act with check
levels.the_agent_may: Carry out the fix and close the ticket. Every closure is checked afterwards.
levels.a_case_is_checked_by: A check of every closed ticket: did the fix hold, was the requester entitled, does the record match what was done.

levels.name: Act alone
levels.the_agent_may: Carry out the fix and close the ticket. A sample of closures is checked afterwards.
levels.a_case_is_checked_by: The same check, on a sample.

rules._note: All assumptions. 'window' is how many of the latest checked cases of a type count.

start._note: Where each type stands on the first day of the ladder. The four types that the suite's own agent already closes alone start at 'act with check': everything is checked until the evidence says otherwise.

ceiling._note: The highest level a type may ever reach, whatever the evidence. Types that touch identity are never worked alone; a change of recovery contact is always carried out by a person. These are company rules, not thresholds.
